reasoning: Recent information does not show any fresh general-election head-to-head polling for either the presidential or Senate race in Rhode Island within the last 45 days, but structural data and a new in-state survey confirm a very strong Democratic environment. Cook PVI lists Rhode Island as around D+8 statewide, and an August 2026 Pell Center/Salve Regina poll finds Democratic Senator Jack Reed with about 61% support in the primary, indicating he is overwhelmingly favored and reinforcing the expectation of a large Democratic margin in November even though no explicit general-election margin was reported.[3][2][5] Prediction/forecast-style material and market commentary further emphasize that the 2026 Senate race is considered almost certain to go Democratic, with expected victory margins in the mid-teens or higher.[7][10][11]
